## 3. Apply reviewed organism mappings

The source may describe the same organism using several labels, including
older names and resistance or morphotype qualifiers. Join the existing dbt
reference tables to attach standardized identities and reporting groups.
Using the same reference files keeps the R and SQL reporting definitions
aligned.

Retain the original `organism` field and one record per original source
label on each culture. Resistance will be evaluated for those observations
before labels are consolidated into reporting populations.

### 3.1 Load the organism reference tables

Use the organism dictionary and Gram classification CSVs already stored in
`dbt/seeds/`. The relative path below assumes the same working directory as
your existing `../data/raw/` path. Change `seed_dir` if necessary.

```{r load-organism-reference-tables}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

seed_dir = "../dbt/seeds"

organism_mapping =
  read_csv(
    file.path(seed_dir, "organism_mapping.csv"),
    col_types = cols(
      .default = col_character(),
      include_primary_summary = col_integer()
    ),
    na = "",
    trim_ws = FALSE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(organism_reporting_group, source_qualifier),
      ~ na_if(str_trim(.x), "")
    ),
    has_reviewed_mapping = TRUE
  )

organism_reporting_groups =
  read_csv(
    file.path(seed_dir, "organism_reporting_groups.csv"),
    col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
    na = "",
    trim_ws = FALSE
  )
```

`organism_standardized` identifies the reviewed organism name.
`organism_reporting_group` identifies the group used in the final report;
for example, related source identifications can share a reporting complex.
`source_qualifier` retains information such as a source MRSA designation.
Those source qualifiers remain traceable, but AST evidence will determine
the resistance classifications used by this pipeline.

### 3.2 Attach standardized identities and Gram groups

Match each original organism label exactly to the dictionary, then attach
the reporting group's Gram classification. The `left_join()` operations
retain unmatched observations for review. Each reference table must supply
at most one match, preventing the joins from multiplying records.

```{r map-organism-observations}
mapped_organisms =
  culture_organisms %>%
  filter(!is.na(cohort_id)) %>%
  left_join(
    organism_mapping,
    by = c("organism" = "organism_source"),
    na_matches = "never",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    has_reviewed_mapping = coalesce(has_reviewed_mapping, FALSE),
    mapping_status = if_else(
      has_reviewed_mapping,
      mapping_status,
      "unmapped"
    ),
    include_primary_summary = coalesce(include_primary_summary, 0L)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    organism_reporting_groups,
    by = "organism_reporting_group",
    na_matches = "never",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )
```

`has_reviewed_mapping` indicates whether the source label matched the
dictionary. The `include_primary_summary` flag records the reference table's
reporting policy; it does not yet determine the final patient population.
No organism observations are consolidated at this stage.

### 3.3 Review mapping coverage

The previous stage contained 133,246 culture-organism observations across
the three cohorts. This mapping step should retain that count. Review the
unmatched labels and the records enabled for primary reporting that lack a
Gram classification. An unmatched label may be outside the intended report
scope; review its identity and reporting purpose before extending the
dictionary.

```{r check-organism-mapping}
mapping_check =
  mapped_organisms %>%
  summarise(
    culture_organism_records = n(),
    distinct_source_labels = n_distinct(organism),
    matched_records = sum(has_reviewed_mapping),
    unmapped_records = sum(!has_reviewed_mapping),
    primary_reporting_records = sum(include_primary_summary == 1L),
    primary_records_missing_gram = sum(
      include_primary_summary == 1L & is.na(gram_stain_group)
    )
  )

unmapped_labels =
  mapped_organisms %>%
  filter(!has_reviewed_mapping) %>%
  count(organism, name = "culture_organism_count", sort = TRUE)

print(mapping_check, width = Inf)
print(unmapped_labels, n = 20)

mapped_organisms %>%
  count(
    mapping_status,
    include_primary_summary,
    name = "culture_organism_count",
    sort = TRUE
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

The resulting `mapped_organisms` data frame retains the culture identifiers
and original labels alongside standardized organism information. The next
stage will combine these observations with `ast_endpoints` to evaluate
resistance phenotypes.
